appropriate: a solid figure block sitting on a double rule reads as a ruled-off total, and the title-case book serif suits the Everyman/Sage pair; still, someone has to tell you it's a total rather than a page of text
distinctive: nothing like it among the five competitors and it stands out from the circles and triangles in the phone grid, but a slab over two bars is the stock 'document/text' UI glyph, so the details differ while the silhouette stays generic
simple: one rounded slab and two horizontal rules; you could redraw it from memory in seconds
legible: the slab and rules hold at 32 and 24 px; at 16 px the two rules close up into one dark bar, so the double rule is lost but the silhouette survives; 'Clear Ledger' reads in every header lockup
adaptable: black, reversed, one-colour 64 and 32 px, the green app tile, the avatar and the dark header all hold up with no tints; no motion logic is shown
timeless: no trend shapes: plain rules and a conventional book serif with no reverse stress; it would have looked the same ten years ago
universal: the mirrored panel matches the original; rotated 90 degrees it reads faintly as a pause sign or battery icon
clear: unsearched: block-over-lines marks like this are common as 'notes', 'document' and 'list' app icons; I know of no bookkeeping competitor using it, but there are similar marks in other categories
congruent: level, symmetric, static, dark warm ink green on paper and a title-case serif all match the targets; the slab is heavier than the light-to-medium weight the name's sound asks for, and there is no page frame
system: the horizontal lockup, symbol, app icon, avatar and size ladder are shown, but there's no stacked lockup, and the 16 px tier is a straight scale-down rather than its own drawing
